Python API reference¶

Run scripts from the checkout root or install the project first. Start with Output and Python API for the state and callback conventions. These signatures are imported from the current source, not copied from the former scalar interface.

Constitutive kernels¶

Array constitutive kernels. Cauchy stress uses tension-positive signs.

Experimental scalar implementations are retained in legacy/constit_scalar.py. Kernels update history and dstress; update_stress selects the integration scheme.

constit.bingham(mp, material, params)¶

Bi-viscosity Bingham fluid; gamma = sqrt(2 D’:D’), viscosities in Pa s.

constit.dp(mp, material, params)¶

Cohesionless, perfectly plastic Drucker-Prager solid.

constit.dp_rate(mp, material, params)¶

Linear Perzyna Drucker-Prager solid; t_star is a relaxation time (s).

constit.elastic(mp, material, params)¶

Compressible neo-Hookean Cauchy stress, with reference prestress.

Reference energy density:

W0 = G/2 (J^(-2/3) tr(F F^T)-3) + K/2 (ln J)^2
W0 += S0:(F^T F-I)/2

The reference prestress S0 is the input stress at F=I. The law recovers isotropic linear elasticity for small increments around an unstressed state.

constit.linear_mu(mp, material, params)¶

Dense flowing linear mu(I) law, with finite effective-viscosity cap.

constit.pouliquen(mp, material, params)¶

Bounded mu(I) flowing law using engineering shear rate and true density.

No grid-occupancy density cutoff. The finite cap regularises the zero-rate limit. At zero confinement, I is undefined (stored as zero), mu uses its infinite-I limit for nonzero flow, and frictional stress vanishes.

constit.update_stress(mp, material, params)¶

Objective updated mechanics; historical integration is opt-in legacy mode.

constit.validate_material(material, mechanics='updated')¶

Physical parameter domain for the newly restored laws (scalar SI inputs).

constit.viscous(mp, material, params)¶

Newtonian fluid with positive bulk dissipation and standard bulk modulus.

constit.von_mises(mp, material, params)¶

Perfect J2 plasticity; yield_stress (Pa), or sqrt(3)*legacy k.

Segregation operators¶

Conservative central-upwind segregation on the MPM nodal control volumes.

ax=0 denotes x and ax=1 denotes y. Face fluxes transport species mass; concentration increments are obtained by dividing by participating nodal mass.

integrators.KT2_flux(phi, G, P, ax)¶

Physical concentration flux, for inspection on a padded spatial array.

Diffusion is a flux itself, not a velocity to be multiplied by phi again. The timestep uses reconstructed face states via _face_transfers below.

integrators.segregation_update(P, G, particles=None)¶

Return the conservative grid increment and optional particle exchanges.

Interpolation and affine transfer geometry¶

Complete tensor-product particle/grid stencils on a rectangular grid.

Quadratic cardinal B-splines use linear ghost-value extrapolation at physical edges. In the outer half-cell this reduces to linear weights, remains C1 at the join, and preserves nonnegative weights, partition, and linear completeness. Periodic x support retains unwrapped offsets but deposits to unique seam nodes.

interpolation.affine_matrix(affine_momentum, weights, offsets)¶

B D^+ in the resolved 2D support; no inverse-mass or arbitrary ridge.

interpolation.stencil(position, P, G)¶

Return nodes, weights, spatial gradients, and node-minus-particle offsets.

Deformation and volume evolution¶

Updated-Lagrangian kinematics with a rotation-preserving exponential map.

Diagnostics and timestep estimates¶

Run-time inventories and discrete work accounting; no hidden energy correction.

class diagnostics.Diagnostics(P, L)¶

Compact history; boundary/inlet budgets and residuals remain explicit.

External and constraint work use midpoint grid velocities. Residual includes transfer/time integration error and, for rate-form plastic/fluid laws, the difference between their quadratic elastic-energy estimate and exact energy. Periodic angular momentum requires an unwrapped domain, and is diagnostic only here. Prescribed rigid motion is externally controlled.

Conservative explicit timestep estimates, reported separately by mechanism.
